offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

evidence.shows: The symptom is real. posted_exactly_once fails with 7 events booked 2 or 3 times, and matches_provider is off by +$493.23. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider, so only the ledger is wrong.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 10:40:48 with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17s before the alert. No other service changed since 10:39:22.
ledger-consumer booked evt_000308 three times, from offsets 100, 101 and 103 on provider-events partition 0, between 10:41:02 and 10:41:04.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, matching those offsets. These are redeliveries of the same event, and the ledger should have deduplicated them.
evt_000251 was booked twice, at 10:40:49.0 and 10:40:49.7 from offsets 73 and 76, right after the naive-handler deploy.
ledger-consumer logs only 'posted' with no dedup or skip messages, which fits a handler that does not check event_id.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 10:40:48 deploy, which should restore its idempotent handler, to stop new duplicate postings. Then, as a separate approved data repair, reverse the extra ledger transactions. Keep the first transaction id for each event and reverse the rest: 255, 265, 272, 273, 297, plus the extras for evt_000261's set, evt_000298 and evt_000308 (two extras). Afterwards, rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating ledger-consumer pauses ledger booking briefly. Kafka holds the events, so lag builds and then drains. payment-confirmer and payments-api are not touched. Until the data repair runs, the ledger stays $493.23 off, because a rollback repairs nothing already booked. Events redelivered during the naive period stay doubled until they are reversed.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back handler misbehaves, for example by stalling or rejecting events, redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings. Events wait in Kafka under its consumer group and are not lost. Any data-repair reversals can be undone by reversing the reversal transactions.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 10:40:48 ledger-consumer was redeployed with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler books a ledger transaction for every Kafka message and never checks whether the event_id was already posted. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so webhook-receiver can put the same event on provider-events more than once. A correct handler skips those copies. The naive one books each copy. evt_000308 was queued and booked 3 times, and six other events were booked twice. The extra payment postings put provider_clearing $493.23 ahead of the provider. The doubled refund (evt_000288) pulls pay_000217 below the provider's figure. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double entry. Payments and refunds still match the provider, so the damage is limited to the ledger. Still open: why the provider retried these webhooks. A slow acknowledgement or the container recreation are likely causes, but the ledger is meant to absorb retries either way.
